source.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

record.file_problem: Complete paper text, including appendices and numeric tables, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests capacity-dependent generalization and a second descent in LoRA rank sweeps and from-scratch ResNet-18 width sweeps, extending the capacity-sweep finding to pretrained adapters and noisy image and text classification.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization or generalization on clean natural labels. Results cited from other work are not rows. Its main experiments use label noise; the from-scratch ResNet control directly sweeps width and reports test risk after interpolation.
record.test_reason: The from-scratch ResNet-18 and transformer width sweeps test V2 in new architectures and noisy-data settings. The main LoRA experiments vary adapter rank rather than network width and do not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that extending LoRA sweeps beyond full rank reveals a second descent, but no measured post-peak rank that saves parameters matches module-matched dense fine-tuning. DeiT-Tiny first meets their equivalence criterion at rank 3d, using four times dense's projection weights, under a shared learning rate. Rank-one LoRA beats dense on three vision backbones. Their width controls show complete recovery for ResNet-18 and limited recovery for the transformer.
record.recipe_differences: Capacity is swept through LoRA rank in pretrained, noisy-label fine-tuning and through width in from-scratch ResNet-18 and transformer controls; these are not the original one-hidden-layer ReLU setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with architecture (ResNet-18 versus transformer and across tested backbones), training budget, label-noise rate, augmentation, data size, learning rate, weight decay, adapter scaling and placement, model selection, and sweep endpoint.

fits_no_version.finding: DeiT-Tiny LoRA NLL rises from 1.571 at rank one to 2.102 at rank 64, then falls to 1.953 at four times model width; the shape changes with training budget and validation selection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adapter-rank sweeps in noisy pretrained fine-tuning can show a second descent whose location and extent depend on training and selection.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 175 LoRA runs, test NLL correlates more strongly with training NLL than nominal rank; the ordering persists after controlling for training budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-fit status tracks test risk more closely than nominal adapter rank in these noisy fine-tuning runs.

record.problems: The main comparisons use small seed counts (often three); intervals with three seeds are described as descriptive. Several appendix results are figure-only in the supplied text. Experiments concern noisy-label classification and do not establish the broader natural-label/random-label claim.
record.rows_left_out: Kept representative rank-sweep points and the explicitly described width-control outcomes, rather than one row for every rank. Additional numeric rank-by-rank results appear in Tables 1, 3, 8, 10, 11, 13, and 14 and Appendix C; details not extracted include most ranks, backbone comparisons, noise-rate and augmentation panels, dense-capacity axes, and optimization-coordinate interventions. They do not directly test the named width claim except where identified above.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting fixed random labels with natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.

The original one-hidden-layer ReLU setting, training to convergence without explicit regularization, and ResNet classification-error trends are not established. These controls use AdamW with weight decay and fixed epoch budgets.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or ranking against norm and margin measures.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining against random-removal controls.

missing.what: Transformer classification accuracy and training fit across widths: test accuracy is 9.8%, 10.7%, 12.3%, 12.2% and 12.2% at widths 48, 96, 192, 288 and 384; training accuracy is 99.7% at 48 and 100% thereafter. These directly address V2's test-error wording and identify the interpolating regime.

record.verdict_notes: Being below the pre-peak valley or matching dense fine-tuning is not required by V2. Its relevant prediction is improvement with additional width after fitting the training data. LoRA rank, dense-versus-adapter comparisons, stable rank and factor-conditioning interventions do not measure that prediction.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label test accuracy.
Tests ResNet-18 width sweeps on noisy CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 subsets, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; also tests LoRA rank, not width.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples or compare retraining with random-example removal.

rows.subject: DeiT-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: LoRA rank sweep on fused qkv projections in the last six blocks; 20% symmetric label noise; 40 epochs
rows.note: Lowest-risk rank; not a width sweep.
rows.check: Adapter rank is not network width. A single rank's NLL also cannot establish a post-interpolation trend.

rows.subject: DeiT-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: LoRA rank sweep under the same noisy-label setup
rows.note: Risk rises to its peak as ranks acquire the ability to fit noisy labels.
rows.check: This is a LoRA rank comparison. Rising risk from the pre-interpolation valley to the peak would not itself reverse V2, which concerns widening beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: DeiT-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: LoRA rank sweep extended beyond full rank
rows.note: Risk descends after the peak but remains above the r=1 valley.
rows.check: Redundant adapter factors beyond full rank do not widen the network. Remaining above the pre-peak valley is also not, by itself, a failure of post-interpolation improvement.

rows.subject: DeiT-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: LoRA rank sweep at different training budgets
rows.value: Risk is monotone in rank because low ranks have not yet interpolated.
rows.note: Text describes the curve but gives no per-rank values here.
rows.check: Varies adapter rank, with low ranks not yet interpolating. The text explicitly says risk rises monotonically; numerical values are not required to establish that qualitative finding.

rows.subject: DeiT-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: LoRA rank sweep at different training budgets
rows.baseline: 20 epochs: no peak reported; 80 epochs: r=32
rows.check: Peak location is a diagnostic rather than a standalone generalization result, and the axis is adapter rank.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Width sweep on noisy CIFAR-10 using the same pipeline
rows.measure: test NLL relative to pre-peak valley
rows.value: Second descent finishes 0.196 nats below the valley, in every seed.
rows.note: Direct width-sweep result; widths and budgets are listed in Table 2.
rows.check: The reported NLL descent supports the widening trend, but does not directly establish falling classification error. Add the 120-epoch budget and Table 5 values: valley 2.560 at width multiplier 2, peak 5.304 at 4, endpoint 2.364 at 32. Convergence is not demonstrated.

source_check.correct: For V2's classification-error claim, state=cannot_determine. The NLL descent is observed: reported endpoint improvement 0.196 nats below the pre-peak valley in every seed; 120 epochs; Table 5 valley 2.560 at width multiplier 2, peak 5.304 at 4, endpoint 2.364 at 32.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3; Table 2, E5; Appendix B.2, Figure 7; Table 5, E5.
source_check.problem: NLL improvement alone cannot establish V2's falling classification error; the linked state overstates what this measure shows.

rows.subject: 12-block transformer, width w
rows.operation_detail: Width sweep on noisy CIFAR-100; same 5,000-example subsets and noise draws as fine-tuning axes
rows.note: The paper identifies this as a final-ascent regime; width values and train/test accuracy appear in Appendix B.2.
rows.check: Include the post-peak values: NLL falls from 7.439 at width 96 to 6.809 at 192, then rises to 6.843 and 6.879 at 288 and 384. Every post-peak width has 100% training accuracy. Rec below one alone does not refute V2; the later increase directly qualifies continued improvement.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix B.2, transformer width table and validity criteria; Table 5, E28.

rows.subject: DeiT-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: LoRA rank sweep with 20% label noise, compared across rank and training fit
rows.measure: Correlation of test NLL with nominal rank and train NLL
rows.value: ρ=0.40 with nominal rank; ρ=−0.86 with train NLL
rows.note: This is a correlation across runs, not a direct measure of width-sweep generalization.
rows.check: Correlations across LoRA runs do not measure a network-width effect. The pool holds backbone, prior and sample size fixed, but varies rank, epoch, learning rate and scaling.

rows.subject: DeiT-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: LoRA rank sweep with learning rate, weight decay and stopping epoch selected separately for each rank

conditions.value: selected checkpoints all stop before interpolation

rows.measure: test NLL relative to r=1 valley

rows.uncertainty: std over 3 fresh seeds; seed differences reported in text

relationships.condition: From-scratch ResNet-18 width sweeps on noisy CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 under fixed training budgets
relationships.reason: R6 and R7 report post-peak NLL falling below the pre-peak valley in every seed, by 0.196 and 0.658 nats respectively; this supports the risk trend with classification-error and convergence qualifications.
relationships.display_finding: After the peak, negative log-likelihood fell below the low reached before the peak by 0.196 and 0.658 nats in every seed. This did not establish an improvement in classification error or convergence.

relation.reason: The study's own transformer width sweep reports post-interpolation classification accuracy, including incomplete improvement and a wider-model decline. LoRA rank sweeps do not directly test network-width V2.

tranche.reason: The from-scratch width controls introduce new architectures, noisy datasets, AdamW, weight decay and fixed budgets. The transformer reports classification accuracy bearing on V2; these are extensions beyond the original shallow-network recipe.

source_check.notes: The ResNet synthesis statements correctly describe related NLL findings, but those findings do not establish V2's classification-error trend. Section 3 reports R7's improvement as 0.658 nats; the rounded Table 5 cells subtract to 0.659.
